title: Flávio Bolsonaro and family to receive U.S. visas after leaving Brazil, State Department says
summary: Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro has left the country for the United States after losing Sunday's presidential election, three sources said on Tuesday afternoon, with the U.S. State Department due…

image.caption: Brazilian presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, of the Liberal Party, looks on as he speaks after losing the presidential runoff election in Brasilia, Brazil, on Oct. 25. Sources say he has left the country for the U.S. after losing the election and refusing ‌to comply with a Supreme Court order

blocks.text: World

Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro has left the country for the United States after losing Sunday's presidential election, three sources said on Tuesday afternoon, with the U.S. State Department due to grant him and his family entry visas.
Trump said he would approve of Bolsonaro coming to the U.S.
Bolsonaro, who has yet to concede to leftist incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, left Brazil after refusing to comply with a Supreme Court order to surrender his passports.
The ruling relates to a money laundering probe in which he denies wrongdoing.
The location of Bolsonaro, his wife and two daughters was not immediately clear. One source close to the family said they had landed in Florida, but declined to say where.
"The State Department will issue visas to Flávio Bolsonaro and his family and allow them entry into the United States," a senior State Department official said.
Trump praises Bolsonaro
Meanwhile, U.S. President Donald Trump said early Wednesday that he would approve of Bolsonaro coming to the U.S., calling him and his family "fine people."
"The election was really strange, and I thought it was terrible," Trump told reporters at Joint Base Andrews, Md., after returning from campaigning in Texas.
He stressed again, however, that he did not endorse a candidate in Brazil's election. Asked about Bolsonaro's whereabouts, Trump said he had heard he was in Argentina.

A polarized Brazil heads to presidential vote Sunday with economy, corruption top of mind

blocks.text: Bolsonaro's departure for the United States threatens ​to deepen a rift between the two most populous nations in the Americas. Lula has accused Washington of colluding with the Bolsonaros to put them ​back in power, and Reuters reported ahead of Sunday's election on a U.S. State Department campaign ⁠to restore them to office.

Bolsonaro was ​favoured to win Sunday's presidential election but ended ​up losing in a shock result to leftist incumbent Lula. On Monday, he was given 24 hours ​to hand in his passports as part of a money laundering ⁠probe in which he denies ⁠wrongdoing — but that deadline has ‌now lapsed, two other sources said, leading to his documents being cancelled.
Lula wins Brazil’s presidential election run-off
Flávio Bolsonaro's father, former president Jair Bolsonaro, also went to the United States after refusing to concede losing to Lula in 2022.

He eventually returned to Brazil ⁠but was later given a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup. His son has yet to officially concede defeat, saying Sunday he would seek the annulment of the ‌result over alleged voter irregularities. But his Liberal Party said on Monday it acknowledged Lula's victory.
A senior Brazilian Federal Police official said Bolsonaro has not exited the country via any regular migration point.
Right-wing influencer Paulo ​Figueiredo, who serves as a sort of unofficial spokesperson for the Bolsonaro family, declined to answer questions about ⁠Bolsonaro's whereabouts.
"After months of intense work that has been unfairly thwarted, I am not ⁠in the mood to speak to the press," he said. "If ⁠I have any comments to ​make on any matter, I will get in touch."
Supporters of Bolsonaro react to early presidential runoff results in Rio de Janeiro on Oct. 25. (Silvia Izquierdo/The Associated Press)
Eduardo Bolsonaro, Bolsonaro's younger brother who ​lives in the U.S., ⁠said ahead of the vote that an election loss would require a move.
"If my brother does not win, I'm in favour that he would leave the country," he told U.S.-based podcaster Steven Crowder this month.
